description: We are university students passionate about AI, engineering, programming, and space technology. Our name, Aetheron, represents our curiosity about the unknown and our ambition to explore new ideas. For NASA Space Apps, we aim to combine our diverse skills, use NASA’s open data, and build practical solutions through creativity, teamwork, and continuous learning
summary: Echo of SARs is a satellite-based forest monitoring project focused on Central Bago Yoma, Myanmar. Our project uses Sentinel-2 imagery from April 2020 and April 2026 to compare vegetation greenness through NDVI, with NDMI and NBR as supporting indicators. We also incorporate four months of NASA-ISRO NISAR radar observations into our forest monitoring map. Through an interactive website, users can explore the study area, compare satellite imagery, and visualize changes in vegetation and radar observations. By presenting these observations in an accessible way, we aim to support environmental awareness and further investigation. We do not claim to confirm deforestation, forest degradation, or overall forest health.
details:
Echo of SARs is a satellite-based forest monitoring project focused on Central Bago Yoma, Myanmar. Our project uses Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from April 2020 and April 2026 to observe vegetation changes through the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), with the Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) as supporting information. We also incorporate four months of NASA-ISRO NISAR radar observations to provide another perspective on forest monitoring.

Through our interactive website, users can explore the Bago Yoma study area, compare satellite images from different years, and visualize vegetation changes through interactive maps. The website also presents supporting NDMI information and NISAR radar observations to help users understand the different types of satellite data.

Our goal is to make satellite observations easier to explore and understand, while supporting awareness and monitoring of forest changes. We present what the satellite data shows without claiming to confirm deforestation or forest degradation.
